SC0 B81.summary: The party attends a bullfight, the crowd heckles and cheers, and Rafael surprises Claudio by recruiting Emilio.

speeches.Japanese:
おじいちゃん。スペインに来たら
闘牛見せてくれる約束でしょ？
speeches.English:
Grandpa, you promised to take me 
 to a bullfight when we got 
 to Spain, remember?

speeches.Japanese: ん？　そうじゃったかの？
speeches.English: Hm? Did I now?

speeches.Japanese:
もう！
いっつも話ばっかりで一度も見たこと
ないのよ
speeches.English:
Honestly! You're always talking
 about it, but I've never actually
 seen one!

speeches.Japanese:
みんなもどう
話の種にでもいいでしょ？
ね、行きましょうよ
speeches.English:
How about the rest of you? It'll 
 give us something to talk about, 
 at least. Come on, let's go!

speeches.Japanese:
闘牛か、俺も見たことはないな
面白そうじゃねえか
speeches.English:
A bullfight? Never seen one. 
 Sounds fun.

speeches.Japanese: そうだね。ちょっと寄ってみようか
speeches.English: Sure. Let's take a look.

speeches.Japanese:
へー。やっぱりすごいねー
こんなに人がいっぱいいるよ
speeches.English: Wow! Look at this crowd!

speeches.Japanese:
スペイン王国は今のところ
世界を制しておるのじゃからな
ふふん
speeches.English:
Spain rules much of the world
 now. Ho ho!

speeches.Japanese: じじいが、偉えわけじゃねえだろーが
speeches.English:
Yeah, well, that doesn't make
 you a big shot, old man.

speeches.Japanese:
口の減らんやつじゃ
もっと年寄りを尊敬せんかっ
speeches.English:
Such a sharp tongue! Respect 
 your elders!

speeches.Japanese:
なんか、人気のある
闘牛士が出てるんだって
speeches.English:
They say there's a really popular
 bullfighter performing today.

speeches.Japanese: かっこいい人かも♪
speeches.English: Maybe he's handsome!

speeches.Japanese: ま、俺には負けるだろうがな
speeches.English: He cannot outshine me.

speeches.Japanese: どれどれ
speeches.English: Let's have a look.

speeches.Japanese: わっはっは！
speeches.English: Ha ha ha!

speeches.Japanese: 今日も笑わせてくれよー！
speeches.English: Make us laugh again!

speeches.Japanese:
ええっ？
あれが一番の人気闘牛士？
speeches.English:
Huh? That's the most popular 
 bullfighter?

speeches.Japanese: あれは副闘牛士（ピカドール）じゃ
speeches.English:
That's the picador,
 the matador's assistant.

speeches.Japanese:
ああやって先に牛の体力を奪っておいて
主役の闘牛士（マタドール）が
トドメを刺すんじゃよ
speeches.English:
He wears down the bull first. Then 
 the matador finishes it.

speeches.Japanese: とりゃああーーっ！！
speeches.English: Hyaaah!!

speeches.Japanese:
がはははは！
あのバカ、牛と遊んでやがる！
うひょー！　投げ飛ばしやがった！
speeches.English:
Ha ha! That fool's playing 
 with the bull! Whoa! What a throw!

speeches.Japanese: むんがーーっ！！
speeches.English: Raaah!!

speeches.Japanese: わっはっは！
speeches.English: Ha ha ha!

speeches.Japanese: 早く引っこめーっ！！
speeches.English: Get him out!

speeches.Japanese: おおっ、いよいよ真打ちの登場だ！
speeches.English: Oh! Here comes the star at last!

speeches.Japanese: おおーっ！！
speeches.English: Ooooh!!

speeches.Japanese: 待ってました！
speeches.English: At last!

speeches.Japanese: ひゅーひゅー！
speeches.English: Woo-hoo!

speeches.Japanese: わーわー！
speeches.English: Hooray!

speeches.Japanese: 楽しませてくれよ！
speeches.English: Give us a good show!

speeches.Japanese: ブラーボー！！
speeches.English: Bravo!!

speeches.Japanese: わーわー！
speeches.English: Hooray!

speeches.Japanese: ざわざわ…
speeches.English: Murmur...

speeches.Japanese: …彼、仲間に誘ってみようか？
speeches.English: Ask him to join us?

speeches.Japanese:
おいおい、FI
何を言い出すんだ？
speeches.English:
Hey, FI, what
 are you talking about?

speeches.Japanese: だって、すごかったじゃない？
speeches.English: He was incredible, right?

speeches.Japanese: そりゃあそうだが
speeches.English: Yes, but...

speeches.Japanese: んじゃ、決まり
speeches.English: Then it's settled!

speeches.Japanese: って、おい！　本気か～！？
speeches.English: Wait! Are you serious?!

speeches.Japanese: ねえねえ
speeches.English: Hey!

speeches.Japanese: んー？
speeches.English: Hmm?

speeches.Japanese:
（ずるっ！）
な、何だ～？　おいおい
そ、そっちのほうかよ！
speeches.English:
Whoa! W-wait a second! You meant 
 THAT guy?!

speeches.Japanese:
君は船で大海原に乗り出してみようと
思わないかい？
speeches.English: Would you like to sail the open sea?

speeches.Japanese:
ふね？　ふねかあ。こわそうだなぁ
おいしそうじゃあないしなあ
speeches.English:
A ship? Hmm... Sounds scary. 
 Doesn't sound tasty, either.

speeches.Japanese:
…おいしそうじゃないって…
そりゃそうだけど…。そうだ！
世界中のおいしい物を食べに
行こうよ！
speeches.English:
...Tasty? Well, no, I suppose
 not... Oh, I know! Come try
 delicious food from all over 
 the world!

speeches.Japanese:
おいしいもの？　へへっ
へへへ
speeches.English: Delicious food? Heh heh...

speeches.Japanese:
そうさ。いろんな食べ物があるんだよ
きっとね
speeches.English:
That's right! There must be all
 kinds of food out there!

speeches.Japanese:
そ、そおかあ
いろいろが、いっぱいかあ
じゃあいく！　うみでもどこでも！
speeches.English:
R-really? All kinds, and lots
 of it? Then I'm in! I'll go
 anywhere, even to sea!

speeches.Japanese:
決まったね
じゃあ、名前を教えてもらわなくちゃ
僕は
FI・FA
speeches.English:
It's settled, then!
 What's your name?
 I'm FI FA.

speeches.Japanese:
お、おいらエミリオ・フェローグ
よろしく
speeches.English:
I-I'm Emilio Ferog.
 Nice to meet you.

speeches.Japanese: これからもよろしく。エミリオ
speeches.English: Welcome aboard, Emilio.

SC0 B150.summary: The innkeeper recounts the divination dish’s use, Rafael tries the lotus leaf, and Hans explains the two keys needed for each map.

speeches.Japanese:
おや？
それは『クシャナ朝の大皿』だね
その皿には昔話があるんだよ
知ってるかい？
speeches.English:
Oh? That's a Kushan Platter. 
 There's an old tale about it.
 Do you know it?

speeches.Japanese: どんな話なんですか？
speeches.English: What kind of tale?

speeches.Japanese:
その皿は占いの道具だったらしいよ
皿に水を入れ、浮かべた花や葉で
その年の出来事を占ったんだって
speeches.English:
They say it was for divination.    
 People filled it with water,   
 then floated flowers or leaves 
 to foretell the year's events.

speeches.Japanese:
その占いで『覇者の証』の場所も
分かるといいのになあ…
試しに『枯れないハスの葉』を
浮かべてみよう
speeches.English:
If only it could tell us where 
 the Proof is... Let's try floating 
 the Evergreen Lotus Leaf on
 the water.

speeches.Japanese:
ああっ！？
葉が水を吸って
葉脈に何か浮かんできましたよ！
speeches.English:
Oh! The leaf's soaking up
 the water... Something's appearing 
 in its veins!

speeches.Japanese:
ああっ！？
葉が水を吸って
葉脈に何か浮かんできましたよ！
speeches.English:
Oh! The leaf's soaking up
 the water... Something's appearing 
 in its veins!

speeches.Japanese:
やった！
これがインド洋の『覇者の証』の地図だ！
speeches.English:
We did it! This is the map 
 to the Proof in the Indian Ocean!

speeches.Japanese:
やりましたね
FI！
speeches.English: We did it, FI!

speeches.Japanese:
やりましたね
FI！
speeches.English: We did it, FI!

speeches.Japanese:
おばさんのおかげだよ！
ありがとう！
speeches.English:
It's all thanks to you, ma'am! 
 Thank you!

speeches.Japanese:
『覇者の証』のありかを示す地図は
みな、２つに分かれておるようじゃ
まずは、２つの鍵を見つけることじゃな
speeches.English:
The maps to the Proofs all seem
 to be divided in two. First, 
 you must find the two keys.

speeches.Japanese: 地図の…鍵？
speeches.English: Map... keys?

speeches.Japanese:
２つの鍵がそろい、両者がうまく
組み合さったとき、初めて
『覇者の証』の地図が現れる
というわけじゃ
speeches.English:
Only when you have both keys 
 and combine them properly
 will the map to the Proof appear.

speeches.Japanese:
ということは、７つの証を集めるには
全部で１４個の鍵を集めなければ
いけないってことですね？
speeches.English:
So to collect seven Proofs, we need
 all fourteen keys?

speeches.Japanese: そういうことになるのう
speeches.English: Exactly.

speeches.Japanese:
１４個！？
そいつは大変だな
speeches.English: All 14!? That's tough.

speeches.Japanese:
ふぉ、ふぉ
そんな簡単に見つかるものなら
とっくに誰かが手に入れておるわい
speeches.English:
Ho, ho. Were they easy to find,
 someone would have them already.

speeches.Japanese:
そりゃそうだ。まったく
世の中、うまくできてるよなあ
speeches.English:
Fair point. Nothing ever comes 
 easy, does it?

speeches.Japanese:
FOの者であるな
通るがよい
speeches.English:
You're with FO, I see. 
 You may pass.

speeches.Japanese:
地中海を統べるべき者よ
汝にこれを授く
speeches.English:
You shall rule the Mediterranean.
 I bestow this upon you.

speeches.Japanese: こいつはすげえ！！
speeches.English: Amazing!

speeches.Japanese: パシャ軍が持っていたのかな…
speeches.English:
I wonder if Pasha's forces 
 had this...

speeches.Japanese:
ハイレディン提督は
これを…
speeches.English: Admiral Hayreddin... This...

SC0 B180.summary: The shipwright offers a lesson with an optional refusal, explains sail types and mast behavior, and returns to work.

speeches.Japanese:
そこの提督さん
俺の帆船講座を聞く気はあるかい？
speeches.English: Admiral. Want a sailing lesson?

speeches.Japanese: え？
speeches.English: Huh?

speeches.Japanese:
ここんとこ、ヒマでヒマでしょう
がねえんだ
まあ、人助けとでも思ってさ
speeches.English:
I've been bored out of my skull
 lately. Think of it as doing 
 me a favor.

speeches.Japanese:
私たちを見くびってもらっては
困りますよ
speeches.English: Please don't underestimate us.

speeches.Japanese: ふむふむ、その通り
speeches.English: Hmm, quite right.

speeches.Japanese:
船のことなら
今さら聞くまでもないのであります
speeches.English:
When it comes to ships,
 we're past needing lessons.

speeches.Japanese:
まあ、しょうがねえか
あんたら、船に詳しそうだしな
もっと素人っぽい客を待つとするか
speeches.English:
Fair enough. You look like you know
 your ships. I'll wait for somebody 
 who looks a little greener.

speeches.Japanese:
うんうん、いい心がけだね
あんた、大物になるよ
speeches.English: That's the spirit. You'll go far.

speeches.Japanese:
さて、帆船ってくらいだから
帆は船の命だな
speeches.English: A sailing ship lives by its sails.

speeches.Japanese:
よし。まずは四角帆と三角帆の
違いについて説明しよう
speeches.English:
Let's start with square sails
 and lateen sails.

speeches.Japanese:
四角帆は『スクウェアセイル』とも
いって、船の方向に対して横に
張られた帆、横帆の一種だ
speeches.English:
A square sail is rigged crosswise. 
 That's what makes
 it a transverse sail.

speeches.Japanese:
横帆だから、帆を縦にすることが
できねえ。つまり順風には強いが
逆風のときには最適な角度にする
ことはできねえってわけさ
speeches.English:
A square sail can't turn 
 fore-and-aft. It does well 
 in a following wind. 
 But in a headwind, 
 you can't set it at the best angle.

speeches.Japanese:
三角帆、“通”は『ラテンセイル』って
呼ぶが、四角帆とは逆に、縦に張られて
いて船の方向に対して横に
することができねえ
speeches.English:
Sailors who know their stuff call
 the triangular one a lateen. 
 It's rigged along the ship,
 so unlike a square sail, 
 you can't turn it crosswise.

speeches.Japanese:
逆風のときには、ばっちりの角度に
できるが順風の時にはそれほど
スピードが出ねえのはそういうわけ
だな。…ここまではいいかい？
speeches.English:
You can get just the right angle 
 in a headwind, but you won't go
 as fast with the wind behind you.
 With me so far?

speeches.Japanese: 次は、追加で付けられる帆についてだ
speeches.English:
Next up are the extra sails
 you can add.

speeches.Japanese:
上帆は、正しくは『トップセイル』
といって、各マストの上に取り付ける
小さな横帆のことだ
speeches.English:
Sailors call the upper sail
 a topsail. It's a small square sail
 rigged high on each mast.

speeches.Japanese:
斜帆は『ステイセイル』、各マストの
前に付ける小さな縦帆だ。三角帆の
前には付けられねえ。縦帆どうしだと
重なっちまうからな
speeches.English:
A staysail is a small fore-and-aft 
 sail that goes in front
 of each mast. You can't put one
 in front of a lateen sail. 
 The two would overlap.

speeches.Japanese:
船首帆は、海の男だったら
『スプリットセイル』と呼んでくれ
こいつは、船の舳先に付ける横帆だ
小型の船に取り付けるのはムリだな
speeches.English:
We sailors call the bow sail 
 a spritsail. It's rigged crosswise 
 at the bow, and you can't fit one
 on a small ship.

speeches.Japanese:
船尾帆は、『ジガースパンカー』とも
いう。縦帆だが、小さなマストが１本
増えるようなものだから
大型船にしか付けられねえぜ
speeches.English:
The stern sail is also called
 a jigger spanker. It's rigged
 fore-and-aft, but fitting
 it is like adding a little mast. 
 You can only put one 
 on a large ship.

speeches.Japanese:
さて、マストが２本以上ある船は
追い風よりも、やや斜めの風のほうが
スピードが出るって知ってたか？
speeches.English:
Did you know that with 
 two or more masts, a ship
 goes faster with the wind
 off its rear quarter 
 than with the wind straight astern?

speeches.Japanese: そこのあんた、なぜだか分かるかい？
speeches.English: How about you? Know why that is?

speeches.Japanese:
…ふむ。マストが前後に
並んでいるからですな
speeches.English:
Hmm. Because the masts are lined up
 fore and aft, I suppose.

speeches.Japanese:
そうだ。真後ろからの追い風だと
後ろのマストだけが風を受けて
前のほうにあるマストが役に立たねえ
からな
speeches.English:
Right. With the wind straight
 astern, only the rearmost mast gets
 any wind. The forward masts don't
 help you at all.

speeches.Japanese:
斜め後ろから風を受けたときが
一番速えってわけさ。無論、帆の角度は
合わせねえといけねえがな
speeches.English:
That's why you're fastest
 with the wind coming at an angle 
 from behind. Of course, you still
 have to set your sails to match.

speeches.Japanese: なるほど！
speeches.English: Right!

speeches.Japanese:
おお、今まであまり
気にしてませんでした！
そういうわけだったのですね！
speeches.English:
Oh! I never gave that much thought.
 Now I see why it works!

speeches.Japanese:
付き合ってくれてありがとうよ
さあ、仕事に戻るとするか
speeches.English:
Thanks for hearing me out. Well, 
 back to work.

SC0 B195.summary: Three art buyers disagree about painters and place their orders. The shopkeeper explains the fashion once they leave.

speeches.Japanese: ん？
speeches.English: Hm?

speeches.Japanese: 本当に素晴らしいよ！
speeches.English: Truly wonderful!

speeches.Japanese: そうかね？
speeches.English: You think so?

speeches.Japanese:
ああ、彼は後世に名を残す
芸術家になるね
speeches.English:
I do. He's an artist people
 will remember for generations.

speeches.Japanese: はあ
speeches.English: Ah.

speeches.Japanese:
君も今のうちに彼の作品を
手に入れておくといい
speeches.English:
You should buy his work
 while you can.

speeches.Japanese: 俺は、こっちの方がいいと思うがね！
speeches.English: Well, I think this one's better!

speeches.Japanese:
それも悪くはないが
彼の作品にはかなわないよ
speeches.English: Not bad, but no match for his work.

speeches.Japanese:
何を言っているんだ、君たち
それより、あっちの方が
いい作品に決まっておる
speeches.English:
What are you two talking about?
 That one over there is clearly 
 the finest.

speeches.Japanese:
何と言われても
私は彼の絵を購入する！
speeches.English:
Say what you like. I'm buying
 his painting!

speeches.Japanese:
俺はこの絵を描いた画家のものを
もらうぞ！
speeches.English: I'll take one by this artist!

speeches.Japanese: 私はこちらをもらおう！
speeches.English: And I'll take this one!

speeches.Japanese: 毎度ありがとうございました
speeches.English: Thank you for your business.

speeches.Japanese: バタンッ！
speeches.English: Slam!

speeches.Japanese:
やっと帰ったか
毎度毎度、店の中で言い争うのは
やめてもらいたいな
speeches.English:
Finally, they're gone. I wish
 they'd quit arguing in here
 every time they come in.

speeches.Japanese: 店主、さっきのは何の騒ぎだ
speeches.English: What was that commotion?

speeches.Japanese: あれは、金持ちの道楽さ
speeches.English: Rich folks and their hobbies.

speeches.Japanese: 金持ちの道楽？
speeches.English: Their hobbies?

speeches.Japanese:
ああ、最近絵画を集めるのが
流行ってるのさ
speeches.English:
Yeah. Collecting paintings 
 is all the rage lately.

speeches.Japanese: へえ。高尚な趣味だな
speeches.English: A refined hobby.

speeches.Japanese:
まっ、本当に見る目のあるヤツは
少ないけどな
speeches.English:
Well, hardly any of them 
 have an eye for it.

speeches.Japanese: はっはっはははは、店主も言うね
speeches.English:
Ha ha! 
 You don't mince words, do you?

speeches.Japanese: おおっと、秘密にしといてくださいよ
speeches.English: Oops. Keep it between us, okay?

speeches.Japanese: 分かってるよ
speeches.English: Of course.

speeches.Japanese: バスラで絵画が流行しそうです
speeches.English: Artwork may catch on in Basra.

SC0 B200.summary: The daimyo admires imported glass, asks what it is, and tells the guildmaster to gather it for his collection.

speeches.Japanese: 素晴らしい！　まさに芸術じゃ
speeches.English: Splendid! A work of art, truly.

speeches.Japanese: 仰せの通りにござる
speeches.English: As you say.

speeches.Japanese:
これほど素晴らしい品であるからには
さぞ名の通った職人が作ったので
あろうな
speeches.English:
A piece this fine must be
 the work of a master craftsman.

speeches.Japanese: さようでございます
speeches.English: Indeed.

speeches.Japanese:
うーむ
このような物が流行しておったとは
全く知らなんだ
speeches.English:
Hmm. I had no idea such things 
 had come into fashion.

speeches.Japanese: これは、何というものじゃ？
speeches.English: What is it called?

speeches.Japanese: ギヤマン（ガラス）にござりまする
speeches.English: It's called giyaman. Glass.

speeches.Japanese: ふーむ。ギヤマンとな
speeches.English: Hmm. Giyaman, you say.

speeches.Japanese:
よしっ、わしの収集に加える
街中のギヤマンを集めてまいれ
speeches.English:
Very well! 
 I'll add it to my collection.
 Go and bring me all
 the giyaman in town.

speeches.Japanese: ははっ、御意のままに
speeches.English: At once. As you command.

speeches.Japanese: 大坂でガラスが流行しそうです
speeches.English: Glass may catch on in Osaka.

SC0 B201.summary: A guildmaster and shopkeeper talk about porcelain. Two bystanders see a chance to profit from the demand.

speeches.Japanese:
この間、やっとあれを
手に入れましたよ
speeches.English:
I finally got my hands on
 it the other day.

speeches.Japanese: おお、陶磁器ですか
speeches.English: Oh, the china?

speeches.Japanese:
ええ、思ったとおり
最高の品でしたよ
speeches.English:
Yes. It was every bit as fine
 as I'd hoped.

speeches.Japanese:
素晴らしい。ひとつ、拝見させて
いただきたいですな
speeches.English:
Splendid. I should very much like
 to see it.

speeches.Japanese:
どうぞどうぞ
ぜひ、拙宅まで足をお運びください
speeches.English:
Of course! Please, do come 
 by my home for a look.

speeches.Japanese:
それにしても、最近の陶磁器収集の
流行で良い品が手に入りにくく
なりましたね
speeches.English:
With everyone collecting china 
 these days, it's getting harder
 to find a good piece.

speeches.Japanese:
流行というだけで
価値の分からん輩が
買いあさってるらしいですな
speeches.English:
So I hear. People who don't know 
 what any of it is worth
 are buying it up 
 just because it's fashionable.

speeches.Japanese: いい迷惑ですよ
speeches.English: What a nuisance.

speeches.Japanese: 全くその通りですな
speeches.English: Exactly.

speeches.Japanese: おい、あそこの男たちを見てみろ
speeches.English:
Hey, take a look at those men
 over there.

speeches.Japanese: あの２人連れか？　どうした
speeches.English: Those two? What about 'em?

speeches.Japanese:
こないだ、全く値打ちのねえ陶磁器を
嘘みたいな値で購入してくれたぜ
speeches.English:
The other day they paid me 
 a ridiculous price for some china
 that wasn't worth a thing.

speeches.Japanese:
へえ、お得意さんじゃねえか
そいじゃ、懐もさみしいことだし
声掛けてみるかい？
speeches.English:
Well, well. Good customers, huh? 
 I'm a little short on cash.
 Why don't we go talk to them?

speeches.Japanese: いいねえ
speeches.English: I like the sound of that.

speeches.Japanese: 決まりだ。行こうぜ
speeches.English: That settles it. Come on.

speeches.Japanese: だんなぁ
speeches.English: Sir!

speeches.Japanese:
ハンブルクで
陶磁器が流行しそうです
speeches.English: China may catch on in Hamburg.

SC0 B207.summary: Two customers follow a smell and order the barkeep’s cheese dish. They enjoy it and expect it to catch on.

speeches.Japanese:
あれ？
何か、いい匂いがしないか？
speeches.English: Something smells good, doesn't it?

speeches.Japanese: くんくん…そうだな
speeches.English: Sniff, sniff... Yeah, I do.

speeches.Japanese: おい、親父こりゃ何の匂いだ
speeches.English: Hey, barkeep! What's that smell?

speeches.Japanese:
これかい？　うちの名物料理さ
チーズたっぷりで、おいしいよ！
speeches.English:
That's our house specialty. Loaded 
 with cheese, and it's delicious!

speeches.Japanese: 本当にうまいのか？
speeches.English: Really that good?

speeches.Japanese: 当たり前のこと聞いちゃいけないよ
speeches.English:
What kind of question is that? 
 Of course it is!

speeches.Japanese: じゃ、俺たちにも１つ頼むよ
speeches.English: Then bring us one.

speeches.Japanese:
はいはい。ちょっとだけお待ちを
すぐにお持ちしますよ
speeches.English:
You got it. Just a moment. 
 I'll bring it right out.

speeches.Japanese: はい、お待ちどう
speeches.English: Here you go. Thanks for waiting.

speeches.Japanese: おっ、本当に早いね
speeches.English: Oh, that really was quick.

speeches.Japanese:
まあ、だまされたと思って
まずは食ってみな
speeches.English: Just trust me and take a bite.

speeches.Japanese: そうだな
speeches.English: Sure.

speeches.Japanese: モグモグ
speeches.English: Munch, munch.

speeches.Japanese: モグモグ
speeches.English: Munch, munch.

speeches.Japanese: うっめぇーーー！
speeches.English: Oh, that's good!

speeches.Japanese:
こりゃ、いけるよ！
すげえ！
speeches.English: This is good! It's amazing!

speeches.Japanese: そうだろ！
speeches.English: Told you!

speeches.Japanese: こりゃ、みんなに教えてやらなきゃ！
speeches.English:
We've gotta tell everybody 
 about this!

speeches.Japanese:
ああ！　
親父、この料理はきっと
大流行するぜ！！
speeches.English:
Yeah! Barkeep, this dish is going
 to be a hit!

speeches.Japanese:
ヴェラクルスで
チーズが流行しそうです
speeches.English: Cheese may catch on in Veracruz.

SC0 B216.summary: Jam takes the innkeeper’s suggestion to visit the castle. The guard reports the missing ornament and the scene ends with Jam’s letter.

speeches.Japanese: 退屈だから、どっか行って来るか
speeches.English:
I'm bored. Think I'll go 
 have a look around.

speeches.Japanese:
おばさん、ここらへんで面白い所は
ないのかい？
退屈しのぎに、散歩したいんだ
speeches.English:
Ma'am, is there anything 
 interesting around here? I'm bored 
 and could use a walk.

speeches.Japanese:
そうだねえ、東に行けば
お殿様のお城があるけどねえ
speeches.English: Well, the lord's castle lies east.

speeches.Japanese:
お城…？　ああ、キャッスルか！
いいねえ、この国の城でも見に行くか
speeches.English:
A fortress...? Oh, a castle! Sounds
 good. I'll go see what castles look
 like here.

speeches.Japanese:
ジャム、どこに行ってたんだよ！
捜したじゃないか！
speeches.English:
Jam, where have you been? I've 
 been looking all over for you!

speeches.Japanese:
わりー、わりー
こいつが重くてよ
speeches.English: Sorry, sorry. This thing's heavy.

speeches.Japanese: な、何これ？　どうしたの？
speeches.English: Wh-what is that? What happened?

speeches.Japanese:
見りゃ分かるだろ？　船首像さ！
正真正銘
メイド・イン・ジャパーンだぜ！
speeches.English:
Can't you tell? It's a figurehead! 
 Genuine article, made in Japan!

speeches.Japanese:
この国の連中、船首像ってもんの
使い方を知らねえらしいから
教えてやってきた
そしたら、お礼にってくれたんだ
speeches.English:
Folks here didn't seem to know 
 what to do with a figurehead,
 so I showed them. They gave
 it to me to say thanks.

speeches.Japanese:
へえ…。まあいいや
出発するから早く支度してよ
speeches.English:
Huh... Anyway, we're leaving.
 Hurry up and get ready.

speeches.Japanese:
ああ、分かった
ちょっと待ってくれよ
speeches.English: Yeah, all right. Give me a minute.

speeches.Japanese:
と、殿！　と～のぉ～！
一大事でございます！
speeches.English:
M-my lord! My lord! Something
 terrible has happened!

speeches.Japanese: 何じゃ！　朝からうるさいぞよ
speeches.English:
What is it? What a racket
 this early in the morning.

speeches.Japanese:
シャ、シャチホコが消えて
こ、このような南蛮文字の手紙がぁ～！
speeches.English:
Th-the shachihoko is gone! 
 And there's this letter
 in foreign writing!

speeches.Japanese:
な、なんと、シャチホコが消えた
じゃだと！　それは一大事じゃ！
なんとしても、その盗人を
探し出すのじゃ！
speeches.English:
What? The shachihoko is gone?! 
 This is serious. Find that thief,
 whatever it takes!

speeches.Japanese: 御意にございます！
speeches.English: At once!

speeches.Japanese: 親愛なる日本の領主殿へ
speeches.English: Dear Lord of the Castle,

speeches.Japanese:
あの像は“船首像”っていうんだ
城じゃなくて、船に飾るものだぜ
きっと、中途半端に
伝わっちまったんだろうな
speeches.English:
That statue's a figurehead. It goes
 on a ship, not a castle. Guess 
 somebody only got half the story.

speeches.Japanese:
ああ、礼はいらないぜ、代わりに
１つ余り物をもらっていくからよ
船首像は船１隻に１つずつ、だ
覚えとくといい
speeches.English:
No need to thank me. I'll take 
 a spare instead. 
 One figurehead per ship, 
 remember that.

speeches.Japanese:
じゃあ、元気でな
　　　ジャム・ジャック・ルドワイヤン
speeches.English:
Take care now.
　　　Jam Jack Ludwyan

SC0 B224.summary: The guildmaster asks about Romance of the Three Kingdoms, reacts to different favorite generals, and mentions Zhao Yun’s spear.

speeches.Japanese:
やあ、あんたたち
『三國志演義』を知っているかい？
speeches.English: Know Romance of the Three Kingdoms?

speeches.Japanese:
そうかあ
一度読んでごらんよ、面白いから
speeches.English:
I see. Give it a read sometime.
 It's a lot of fun.

speeches.Japanese:
そうかい、そうかい
おじさんうれしいよ
ところであんたの好きな武将は誰だい？
speeches.English:
Oh, you do? Well, I'm glad to hear 
 it. Who's your favorite general?

speeches.Japanese:
なんと！　おじさんと同じだよ！
あんたとは話が合いそうだな
speeches.English:
Really? He's my favorite too!
 I think you and I will get along.

speeches.Japanese:
長坂橋で阿斗を胸に抱き
曹操軍を単騎で駆け抜くところなんて
最高だね！
speeches.English:
The part at Changban Bridge, where 
 he holds A Dou to his chest
 and rides right through
 Cao Cao's army all on his own? 
 That's the best!

speeches.Japanese:
実はね、噂で聞いたんだけど
この辺りの半島に趙雲が使ってたって
いう伝説の槍があるらしいんだ
speeches.English:
I heard a rumor that Zhao Yun's
 legendary spear might be on
 a peninsula around here.

speeches.Japanese:
おじさんも手に入れたくって、すごく
探したんだが、結局は見つけられ
なかったんだ。あんたたちなら見つけ
られるんじゃないかと思ってね
speeches.English:
I wanted it myself, so I looked
 high and low. Never did find it. 
 I thought you folks
 might have better luck.

speeches.Japanese:
美髭公・関羽が好きなのかい？
おじさんの好きな武将とは違うけど
知勇兼備の烈士だよね
speeches.English:
You like Guan Yu, the lord 
 with the magnificent beard?
 He's not my favorite, but what 
 a warrior. Clever and brave.

speeches.Japanese:
智将・諸葛孔明か…うんうん
あの“出師の表”は泣かせるよな…
おじさんも２番目ぐらいに好きだよ
speeches.English:
Ah, the strategist Zhuge Liang.
 His Memorial on the Expedition 
 brings a tear
 to your eye, doesn't it? 
 He's probably my second favorite.

SC0 B315.summary: A patron relays the rumored curse and the explorers’ disappearance. Rafael and his crew decide to investigate.

speeches.Japanese:
あんたかい？
マスジット＝イ＝シャーに
行ったっていう命知らずは
speeches.English:
Are you the daredevil who went 
 to Masjid-i Shah?

speeches.Japanese:
命知らず？
行ったのは僕たちだけど
…どうかしたんですか？
speeches.English:
Daredevil? We went there, yes. 
 Is something wrong?

speeches.Japanese: いやー、大変なことになってるよ
speeches.English: Oh, it's turned into quite a mess.

speeches.Japanese:
あんたの武勇伝を聞いた探検家たちが
宝物を手に入れようと次々に
モスクに押し寄せたんだが…
speeches.English:
Explorers heard what you'd done and
 started pouring into the mosque, 
 all after the treasure...

speeches.Japanese:
未だに誰一人として戻ってこない
王の呪いにあったっていう噂まで
流れる始末だ
speeches.English:
So far, not one of them has come 
 back. Now there's even talk
 that the king's curse got them.

speeches.Japanese: 呪い！？
speeches.English: A curse?!

speeches.Japanese:
呪いの噂が流れたとたん
今度は誰も近寄らなくなった
行方不明の奴らなんかほったらかしさ
speeches.English:
Once word of the curse got out,
 nobody would go near 
 the place. They've just left 
 those people there.

speeches.Japanese:
あんたが原因でもあるんだし
本当に勇気があるんならもう一度行って
彼らを捜してくれないか？
speeches.English:
You had a hand in starting all 
 this. If you're really that brave, 
 would you go back and look 
 for them?

speeches.Japanese: そんなこと押しつけられてもなあ…
speeches.English: You can't just dump this on us...

speeches.Japanese:
…
でも、やっぱり放っておくわけには
いかないよ。そうだろ？
speeches.English:
...We can't just leave them there, 
 though. Can we?

speeches.Japanese: ま、まあそうだが…
speeches.English: W-well, no, but...

speeches.Japanese:
あれ？　まさか…
呪いが怖いんじゃないよね？
speeches.English:
Wait... You're not scared
 of the curse, are you?

speeches.Japanese:
クラウ？　まさか…
呪いが怖いんですか？
speeches.English:
Clau? You aren't afraid
 of the curse, are you?

speeches.Japanese: バ、バカ言うな！
speeches.English: D-don't be ridiculous!

speeches.Japanese:
僕たちにも、ある意味で責任はあると
思うんだ。もう一度調査に行こう
speeches.English:
I think we're partly responsible.
 Let's go back and find out 
 what happened.

speeches.Japanese:
そ、そうだな
FIの言う
とおりだ。困ってる連中を
置き去りにはできねえぜ！
speeches.English:
Y-yeah, FI's right. We can't 
 leave those people stranded!

SC0 B323.summary: Rafael brings Sakura wine. The barkeep and a patron drink it, then Sakura tells him about Kyoto.

speeches.Japanese:
そう言えば
ワインを買ってくる約束だったな…
speeches.English:
That's right. I promised I'd bring 
 back some wine...

speeches.Japanese: やあ
speeches.English: Hi there.

speeches.Japanese:
あっ、ワインを持って
きてくれたのね！
speeches.English: Ah, you brought the wine!

speeches.Japanese: 飲んでごらんよ
speeches.English: Go on, try it.

speeches.Japanese:
うん！
…
speeches.English: Okay! ...

speeches.Japanese: どう？
speeches.English: Well?

speeches.Japanese:
おいしいわ！！
清酒とはまた違った味なのね！
speeches.English:
It's delicious! It tastes
 so different from sake!

speeches.Japanese: どれどれ
speeches.English: Let's have a taste.

speeches.Japanese: 俺にも飲ませてくれよ
speeches.English: Hey, let me try some too!

speeches.Japanese: あ、あの…
speeches.English: Uh, wait...

speeches.Japanese: おお！　うめえ！
speeches.English: Whoa! That's good!

speeches.Japanese: こりゃあ、いいや！
speeches.English: Now this is good!

speeches.Japanese: あっという間になくなっちゃった…
speeches.English: Gone in no time...

speeches.Japanese:
ごめんなさい！
大切な売り物なのに
speeches.English:
I'm sorry! You were going to sell
 that wine.

speeches.Japanese:
い、いや、いいんだ
それに君が悪いんじゃないよ
speeches.English:
N-no, it's fine. Besides, it wasn't
 your fault.

speeches.Japanese: でも…
speeches.English: But...

speeches.Japanese:
気にしないで
…じゃあさ、今度は君が日本の話を
してくれるかな？
speeches.English:
Don't worry about it. Say, how 
 about you tell me about Japan
 this time?

speeches.Japanese: うん、いいわ！
speeches.English: Sure!

speeches.Japanese:
へえ、エンペラーが住む、京の都か
一度見てみたいな
speeches.English:
So the emperor lives in Kyoto? I'd 
 love to see the capital someday.

speeches.Japanese:
地図があれば、簡単に行けるわ
途中までなら道案内してあげる
speeches.English:
It's easy to get there with a map. 
 I could show you part of the way.

speeches.Japanese:
本当？
じゃあ、今度行ってみようかな
speeches.English: Really? Maybe I'll go, then.

SC1 B58.summary: The townspeople confront Espinosa. The innkeeper reports forced labor, Sera identifies him, and Hodram leaves his fate to the residents.

speeches.Japanese: ひっ、き、貴様ら、何をする！
speeches.English: W-what are you doing?!

speeches.Japanese: こっちへ来な！
speeches.English: Get over here!

speeches.Japanese: ？　…エスピノサ！？
speeches.English: What? Espinosa?!

speeches.Japanese:
FA殿
よくぞこの卑劣漢を倒してくださった
speeches.English:
Well done, FA! You've 
 defeated this scoundrel.

speeches.Japanese:
こ、こんなことをして
タダですむと思っとるのか！
speeches.English:
Y-you think you can get away 
 with this?!

speeches.Japanese: だまりやがれ！
speeches.English: Shut up!

speeches.Japanese: ぐえっ！！　い、いたい！！
speeches.English: Gah! That hurts!

speeches.Japanese:
今までさんざん好き勝手
やってくれたな
speeches.English:
You've been doing whatever 
 you please all this time!

speeches.Japanese: な、何の話だ？
speeches.English: W-what are you talking about?

speeches.Japanese:
てめえ……忘れたとは言わせねえ
俺の親父はてめえにだまされて
家も農地も奪われ一家ともども
行方不明だ！
speeches.English:
Don't pretend you've forgotten! You
 cheated my father out of his house 
 and farmland! He and the rest
 of my family are missing!

speeches.Japanese:
貴様の不正を本国に知らせようとした
私の友達を、事故に見せかけて
殺しおって！
speeches.English:
My friend tried to report
 your corruption back home. 
 You killed them and made it look 
 like an accident!

speeches.Japanese:
あたしの故郷じゃ、たくさんの村人が
あちこちに連れて行かれて
食うや食わずで働かされてる！
speeches.English:
Lots of villagers back home
 have been taken away and forced
 to work all over the place,
 with barely enough to eat!

speeches.Japanese:
人の皮をかぶった
悪魔…ですな
speeches.English: A devil in human skin...

speeches.Japanese:
し、知らん
みんな、バカな部下どもが勝手に
やったことだ
speeches.English:
I-I know nothing about it! 
 Those fools under me did it all on 
 their own!

speeches.Japanese: こ、この野郎…！！
speeches.English: You bastard...!

speeches.Japanese:
どこまでも腐ってやがるぜ…
情状酌量の余地はねえな
speeches.English:
Rotten to the core... There's no 
 excuse for him.

speeches.Japanese: …セラ、この男を知っているか
speeches.English: Sera, do you know this man?

speeches.Japanese: …はい
speeches.English: ...Yes.

speeches.Japanese: ！！　おまえは！？
speeches.English: Y-you?!

speeches.Japanese:
この男…私…高く、売る…
本国、に、送れ、言った
speeches.English:
This man... said... sell me. 
 For a high price. Send me... 
 to his country.

speeches.Japanese: な、何を…！
speeches.English: W-what...?!

speeches.Japanese: 待て、人違いだ！　言いがかりだ！
speeches.English:
Wait! You've got the wrong man!
 That's a false accusation!

speeches.Japanese:
この男…！　弟…仲間
みな、殺した！！
この男！！
speeches.English:
My younger brother... the others 
 with me... He killed them all! 
 This man!

speeches.Japanese:
や、やめろ！　こっこの女！
くそっ！
あの時一緒に殺していれば……
うッ！！
speeches.English:
S-stop! You... Damn it! I should've
 killed you with the others 
 back then... Ugh!

speeches.Japanese: ……言い逃れはできんようだな
speeches.English:
...Looks like you can't talk 
 your way out of this.

speeches.Japanese:
この人でなしめ！
FA殿
こいつ、どうするつもりですか？
speeches.English:
You monster! FA, what 
 are you going to do with him?

speeches.Japanese: 処遇は君たちに任せる
speeches.English: You decide his fate.

speeches.Japanese:
聞いたか！　さあ、来い！
罪をたっぷりと償わせてやる！
speeches.English:
You heard him! Come on! We'll make 
 you pay for what you've done!

speeches.Japanese: たっ、助けてくれ！！
speeches.English: P-please, help me!

speeches.Japanese:
セラ…よく覚えておけ
まだまだ、ああいう西洋人が世界中で
でかいツラをしているのが現実だ…
speeches.English:
Sera... Remember this. 
 There are still Westerners like him
 throwing their weight around all 
 over the world.

speeches.Japanese:
…かく言うこの俺も、彼らと大差は
ないのかもしれんがな
speeches.English: I may be no different from them...

speeches.Japanese:
いいえ…
FI、は…
違う
speeches.English: No... FI... different.

speeches.Japanese: あまり人を過信しないほうがいい
speeches.English: Don't trust people blindly.

speeches.Japanese: FA殿
speeches.English: FA.

speeches.Japanese:
あなたたちを試すようで心苦しいの
ですが、どうしても見つけてきて
いただきたい物があるのです
speeches.English:
I'm sorry to put you to the test,
 but there's something I'd really 
 like you to find and bring back.

speeches.Japanese:
提督は
ソロモン王伝説に関する噂を
ご存じですかな？
speeches.English:
Admiral, have you heard the legends
 about King Solomon?

speeches.Japanese:
その昔、偉大なるソロモン王の
なせる技は、魔王をも操ったと
あります
speeches.English:
Legend has it that long ago, 
 the great King Solomon 
 could command even the demon king.

speeches.Japanese:
噂によれば、その魔王にまつわる武器が
ここよりはるか北西にある、氷の島に
封印された、というのです
speeches.English:
Rumor has it that a weapon 
 linked to that demon king
 was sealed away on an icy island 
 far to the northwest of here.

speeches.Japanese:
覇王の資格を有する者のみが持つ
といわれているその武器を
もしあなたたちが持ち帰ることが
できたら…
speeches.English:
They say only someone worthy 
 of being a conqueror can possess 
 it. If you can bring it back...

speeches.Japanese: 持ち帰ったら？
speeches.English: Then what?

speeches.Japanese:
ある物をお渡ししようと
思っているのです
speeches.English:
Then there's something I'd like
 to give you.

speeches.Japanese: 何だそれは？
speeches.English: What is it?

speeches.Japanese:
今は言えません
無事に戻られてからのお楽しみ
ということで…
speeches.English:
I can't tell you yet. Let's
 keep it a surprise until 
 you return safely.

speeches.Japanese:
ふむ…
魔王の武器か
speeches.English: Hm... The demon king's weapon...

speeches.Japanese:
はるか北西の…氷の島？
アイスランドのことでしょうかね？
speeches.English:
An icy isle far to the northwest...
 Iceland, perhaps?

SC1 B153.summary: A guard lets Hodram pass, and the officiant gives him an object and tells him where to look next.

speeches.Japanese:
FOの者だな
よし、通れ
speeches.English:
You're with FO. All 
 right, go through.

speeches.Japanese:
地中海を統べる者よ
汝にこれを授く
speeches.English:
You who rule the Mediterranean,
 I bestow this upon you.

speeches.Japanese: あなたは…？
speeches.English: You are...?

speeches.Japanese:
長い間、オスマンの支配に
抵抗してきた者じゃよ
speeches.English:
Someone who has long resisted
 Ottoman rule.

speeches.Japanese: では、あなたがセラたちを助けて？
speeches.English:
Then... were you the one who helped
 Sera and the others?

speeches.Japanese:
細かいことは聞かずともよかろう
さあ、それを解いて
早く『証』を探すのじゃ
speeches.English:
There's no need to concern yourself
 with the details. Now, 
 decipher it and find the Proof 
 without delay.

speeches.Japanese:
我らのようにオスマンの支配を
逃れた者たちは他にもおる
トルコにある遺跡を探しなされ
speeches.English:
There are others who escaped 
 Ottoman rule, as we did. Look
 for the ruins in Turkey.

SC2 B135.summary: A desperate customer cannot meet Espinosa’s price. Lil confronts him and Camille backs her decision to oppose him.

speeches.Japanese:
く、薬を…。エスピノサさん
薬を譲ってください…
speeches.English:
P-please... Mr. Espinosa, let me 
 have the drug...

speeches.Japanese: 金は？　持ってきたんでしょうね？
speeches.English: Did you bring the money?

speeches.Japanese: こ、これを…
speeches.English: Th-this...

speeches.Japanese:
ふむ…、１、２、３…。残念ですね
これでは『女神の誘惑』は譲れませんな
お金を作って、出直してください
speeches.English:
Hmm... One, two, three...
 I'm afraid this isn't enough 
 for Goddess' Temptation. Come back 
 when you have more money.

speeches.Japanese:
そ、そんな…
前はこれで足りたじゃないか！
speeches.English: But... this was enough last time!

speeches.Japanese:
前は前です
相場というものは常に変動するのですよ
speeches.English: That was then. Market prices change.

speeches.Japanese:
で、ですが、もう…
土地も何もかも売ってしまい…
speeches.English:
B-but... I've already sold 
 my land... everything...

speeches.Japanese:
そんなことは私には関係ありません
お金がないなら、売れませんよ
どうぞ、お引き取りを
speeches.English:
That's not my concern. No money, 
 no sale. Please leave.

speeches.Japanese: エ、エスピノサさん…
speeches.English: M-Mr. Espinosa...

speeches.Japanese:
早く帰れよ！　エスピノサさんは
目障りだとおっしゃっているんだ！
speeches.English:
Get out! Mr. Espinosa says 
 you're an eyesore!

speeches.Japanese: う、ううっ…
speeches.English: Ugh...

speeches.Japanese:
ふふふ、『女神の誘惑』…
素晴らしい商売ですね
笑いがとまりませんよ
speeches.English:
Heh heh... Goddess' Temptation...
 What a wonderful business! 
 I can't stop laughing!

speeches.Japanese: ちょっと、あんた！
speeches.English: Hey, you!

speeches.Japanese:
おや、これはかわいらしいお嬢さん
あなたも『女神の誘惑』を
お求めですか？
speeches.English:
Well, hello, pretty lady. Are you
 after Goddess' Temptation, too?

speeches.Japanese:
あんたね！　麻薬をばらまいて
みんなを苦しめている
エスピノサってヤツは！
speeches.English:
You're Espinosa! Your drugs
 are ruining lives!

speeches.Japanese:
苦しめている…？　とんでもない！
お嬢さん、それは誤解です。私の
お客様は、みな喜んでいらっしゃる
speeches.English:
Ruining lives? Nonsense! 
 You misunderstand, young lady. 
 My customers are all delighted.

speeches.Japanese:
まあ！　ぬけぬけとそんなことを！
そんな悪徳商売をしていて、よく
恥ずかしくないわね！
speeches.English:
How can you say that with
 a straight face? Aren't you ashamed
 of this rotten business?

speeches.Japanese:
そちらこそ、言いがかりもほどほどに
しなさい！まっとうな取引に口を
挟んでもらっちゃ困る
speeches.English:
You should stop making 
 baseless accusations!
 I won't have you interfering 
 in honest business!

speeches.Japanese:
とぼけてもダメよ！　あたし
全部知ってるんだから！　そっちがその
気なら、こっちにも考えがあるわ！
speeches.English:
Don't play innocent! 
 I know what you're doing!
 If that's your attitude, I've got
 a plan of my own!

speeches.Japanese: ほう、どのような考えです？
speeches.English: Oh? What will you do?

speeches.Japanese:
あんたが麻薬売買をやめないつもりなら
あたしのFOが
あんたの商会を倒してみせるわ！
speeches.English:
Keep selling drugs, and FO
 will bring down your company!

speeches.Japanese:
ふふふ。皆さん、聞きましたか？
なかなか楽しいことを言っていますよ
speeches.English: Heh heh. Hear that? How amusing!

speeches.Japanese:
ひゃははは
お嬢ちゃん、すんげえ冗談だな！
おんもしれえや！
speeches.English: Ha! That's a good one, little girl!

speeches.Japanese:
ふん！
後悔しても遅いんだからね！
speeches.English:
Hmph! By the time you're sorry,
 it'll be too late!

speeches.Japanese:
まあ、せいぜいがんばってください
ふふふ
speeches.English: Well, do your best. Heh heh.

speeches.Japanese:
何があっても、あたし
あのエスピノサ商会を倒すんだから！
カミル、とめてもムダよ！
speeches.English:
Whatever happens, I'm bringing down
 that Espinosa Company! It's no use 
 trying to stop me, Camille!

speeches.Japanese:
ああ。今回は僕もとめないよ
あんな卑劣な男…絶対に許せないよ！
speeches.English:
Yeah. I won't stop you this time.
 That vile man... 
 I can't forgive him!

SC2 B143.summary: The shipwright asks Lil to finance armor research, names the cost, and promises to get to work after she agrees.

speeches.Japanese:
姐さん、ちょいとお願いが
あるんでやすが
speeches.English: Say, can you do me a favor?

speeches.Japanese: なあに？
speeches.English: What is it?

speeches.Japanese:
今度うちの造船所で装甲を追加する
方法を考えてるんですが
どうにも研究資金が足りませんので
speeches.English:
We're researching a way to fit 
 extra armor here at the shipyard,
 but we're short on research funds.

speeches.Japanese:
ふーん
金額によっては考えてもいいけど
speeches.English:
Hmm... I might be able to help,
 depending on how much you need.

speeches.Japanese:
本当ですかい？
さすが姐さんだ！
speeches.English: Really? Now that's generous of you!

speeches.Japanese:
あたしにできることってそれくらい
だもんね。で、いくら必要なの？
speeches.English:
Money's about all I can offer. 
 So, how much do you need?

speeches.Japanese:
３０００００もあれば
完成させられるでしょう
speeches.English: 300,000 gold should do it.

speeches.Japanese:
お安い御用よ
はい、大事に使ってね
speeches.English: Sure. Here, use it wisely.

speeches.Japanese:
ありがたい！
さっそく取りかかりやすぜ！
speeches.English: Thanks! We'll start right away!

SC3 B105.summary: Mao asks Maria to play. His mother fears she has offended Maria, prompting Maria to confide in Xien.

speeches.Japanese: おねーちゃん、あそぼー
speeches.English: Hey, wanna play?

speeches.Japanese:
あら、かわいい。どこの子かしら
ぼうや、おなまえは？
speeches.English:
Oh, how sweet! Whose little boy
 are you? What's your name?

speeches.Japanese:
こら、マオ！！
だ、だめじゃないの
speeches.English: Mao! N-no! You mustn't!

speeches.Japanese: どうしてー？
speeches.English: Why not?

speeches.Japanese:
FA様！
も、申し訳ありません！！
息子の無礼、お、お許しください
speeches.English:
Admiral FA! I-I'm so sorry!
 P-please forgive my son's rudeness!

speeches.Japanese: …かまわないわ
speeches.English: ...It's quite all right.

speeches.Japanese:
あ、ありがとうございます！
二度とこのような真似は
させませんので！
speeches.English:
Th-thank you! I won't ever let him 
 do it again!

speeches.Japanese:
（花と小鳥だけかしらね。私が注ぐ
　愛情に答えてくれるのは…。）
speeches.English:
(Are flowers and little birds
 the only ones who return 
 the affection I give them...?)

speeches.Japanese: FI…
speeches.English: FI...

speeches.Japanese: シエン？
speeches.English: Xien?

speeches.Japanese:
じゃましたかのう
何度も呼んだのじゃが…
speeches.English:
Am I interrupting? I called
 you several times...

speeches.Japanese:
…ごめんなさい。気づかなかったの
考えごとをしていて
speeches.English:
...I'm sorry. I didn't hear you. 
 I was thinking.

speeches.Japanese: 何か…あったか
speeches.English: Has something... happened?

speeches.Japanese:
私…街の人にすごく
恐れられているのね
speeches.English: The people here... So afraid of me.

speeches.Japanese:
私、あの人たちを倭寇の暴虐から
守ろうと、手を尽くしてきた
だけなのに…
speeches.English:
All I've done is try my hardest
 to protect them from the wokou 
 pirates' cruelty...

speeches.Japanese:
…彼らにも
いつかは分かってもらえる
speeches.English: Someday, they will understand.

speeches.Japanese: ねえ、シエン
speeches.English: Xien...

speeches.Japanese:
…父が死んで倭寇と戦うことを
決意したとき、私は鬼になると誓ったわ
speeches.English:
...When my father died 
 and I decided to fight the wokou,
 I swore I would become a demon.

speeches.Japanese:
鬼なら、人に恐がられて当然よ
倭寇の海賊たちに“翔緋鯱”と呼ばれ
実力以上に恐れられていたことも
重々承知しているわ
speeches.English:
Of course people would fear
 a demon. The wokou 
 pirates called me
 the Soaring Scarlet Orca.
 I knew very well they feared me far
 more than my strength warranted.

speeches.Japanese:
鬼なら、人に恐がられて当然よ
倭寇の海賊たちに“翔緋鯱”と呼ばれ
実力以上に恐れられていることも
重々承知しているわ
speeches.English:
Of course people would fear
 a demon. The wokou 
 pirates call me
 the Soaring Scarlet Orca.
 I know very well they fear me far
 more than my strength warrants.

speeches.Japanese:
でも、実際に目の前で脅える街の人の
姿を見たらどうしようもなく
悲しくなって…
speeches.English:
But when I saw the townspeople 
 cowering right in front of me, 
 I felt so terribly sad...
 I couldn't help it.

speeches.Japanese: …つらい思いをさせておるようじゃな
speeches.English: ...This has hurt you deeply.

speeches.Japanese:
こんなこと、話すつもりはなかったん
だけど、シエンが相手だと、つい口が
軽くなってしまうわ
speeches.English:
I didn't mean to talk about this.
 But when it's you, Xien, I find
 myself saying more than I intended.

speeches.Japanese: 今の話は、忘れて
speeches.English: Forget what I said.

speeches.Japanese:
試練はまだ始まったばかりじゃ
強がりだけでやり通せるものでも
あるまい
わしの前では、無理をするな
speeches.English:
Your trials have only just 
 begun. You cannot see
 them through simply
 by pretending to be strong.
 You needn't force yourself when
 you are with me.

speeches.Japanese:
ありがとう。でも大丈夫よ
泣き言を言ってるヒマは
ないんですもの
speeches.English:
Thank you. But I'm all right.
 I don't have time to sit 
 here complaining.

speeches.Japanese:
やるべきことは山のようにあるわ
後でやらなかったことを
後悔するのだけは嫌だから
speeches.English:
There's so much I have to do.
 I don't want to look back
 and regret the things I never did.

speeches.Japanese: FI…
speeches.English: FI...

SC3 B172.summary: Xien and Ian discover a book behind a portrait. The innkeeper says it is unfamiliar and gives them permission to take it.

speeches.Japanese:
イアン殿
この肖像画の御仁をご存知か？
speeches.English:
Ian, do you know the man 
 in this portrait?

speeches.Japanese:
ええ。ロッコ＝アレムケルと言う
昔の航海士ですが
その人がどうかしましたか？
speeches.English:
Yes. Rocco Alemkel, a navigator
 from long ago. Why do you ask?

speeches.Japanese:
いや、なかなか立派な面構えを
していると思ってのう
どういう御仁じゃったのであろうか？
speeches.English:
He has a noble face. 
 What sort of man was he?

speeches.Japanese:
私も、その昔にポルトガルを支えた
人物だということぐらいしか
知らないのです
speeches.English:
I'm afraid all I know
 is that he helped support Portugal 
 in his day.

speeches.Japanese: ガタッ！
speeches.English: Clatter!

speeches.Japanese: 何じゃ？
speeches.English: What?

speeches.Japanese: 見てみましょう
speeches.English: Let's see.

speeches.Japanese:
絵の裏に何か…
本のようですね
speeches.English:
There's something behind 
 the painting... A book, I think.

speeches.Japanese: うむ
speeches.English: Hm

speeches.Japanese:
誰の物でしょうか？
なかなか興味深そうな本ですね
speeches.English:
Whose could it be? It looks
 quite interesting.

speeches.Japanese:
ここの主人に聞いてみるか
主人、宿の主人はおらぬか！
speeches.English:
Let's ask the innkeeper. Hello!
 Anyone there?

speeches.Japanese: はいはい、何だい？
speeches.English: Yes? What is it?

speeches.Japanese:
そこから、このような本が
出てきたのじゃが
speeches.English: We found a book behind the portrait.

speeches.Japanese: どれどれ？
speeches.English: Let's see.

speeches.Japanese:
うーん、見覚えないね
よければ、持っていってもらって
構わないよ
speeches.English: No, never seen it. You may keep it.

speeches.Japanese:
しかし、ただでもらうという
わけには…
speeches.English: But we cannot take it for free.

speeches.Japanese:
気にしなくていいよ。元々ここにあった
ことも知らなかったし
私には関係のなさそうな本だからね
speeches.English:
Don't worry about it. I didn't even
 know it was there, and it doesn't
 look like anything I'd need.

speeches.Japanese:
それならば
ありがたくいただくとしよう
speeches.English: Then we accept it with gratitude.

speeches.Japanese:
そうですね
ありがとうございました
speeches.English: Agreed. Thank you very much.

speeches.Japanese:
そんな、お礼なんていいよ
じゃ、仕事があるから失礼するよ
speeches.English:
No need for thanks.
 Back to work for me.

speeches.Japanese:
とりあえず、この本は
FI様に
渡しましょう
speeches.English: Let's give this book to FI.

speeches.Japanese:
うむ、そうじゃな
それでは、イアン殿から渡しておいて
くれんか
speeches.English: Agreed. Please deliver it for us.

speeches.Japanese: 分かりました
speeches.English: Understood.

speeches.Japanese: うむ
speeches.English: Mm

SC3 B272.summary: The shipwright, gunnery expert and builders work out the armor design. The shipwright asks the party to tell the guildmaster it is ready.

speeches.Japanese: おお！　連れてきてくれたのかい！
speeches.English: Oh! You brought them!

speeches.Japanese: ええ、砲術ならば任せてください！
speeches.English: Yes. Leave gunnery to me!

speeches.Japanese:
じゃあ、造船は
私が相談に乗りましょう
speeches.English: Then let me advise on shipbuilding.

speeches.Japanese: 造船ならば、私をお忘れなく
speeches.English:
Don't forget me when it comes
 to shipbuilding.

speeches.Japanese:
船に関することであれば
私になんでも聞いてくださいませ
speeches.English: Ask me anything about ships.

speeches.Japanese:
えっと、砲身はこんな感じで
火薬はここで爆発します
この力が砲弾に伝わって…
speeches.English:
Well, the barrel is shaped 
 like this. The powder explodes 
 here, and the force is transferred 
 to the cannonball...

speeches.Japanese:
船体はこの角度で組み上げれば
砲撃の威力を分散できますね
speeches.English:
If we build the hull at this angle,
 it should disperse the force 
 of the shot.

speeches.Japanese:
…なるほど
この大砲で攻撃を受けたときは
これだけの被害が出るというわけか
speeches.English:
Ah... So this is the damage
 that cannon would cause.

speeches.Japanese:
この材質ならば、簡単に壊れることは
ないでありましょう！
speeches.English: This material should hold up well!

speeches.Japanese:
ここと、このあたりに
装甲を追加するのが
もっとも効果的ですな
speeches.English:
Adding armor here and here 
 would be most effective.

speeches.Japanese:
おお！
これで、完成だ！
連中をあっと言わせてやるぞ！
speeches.English:
There! It's finished! This'll
 give them a surprise!

speeches.Japanese:
おっと、そうだ！
ギルドの親父に知らせてやってくれ！
ついに、できたってな！
speeches.English:
Oh, right! Tell the guildmaster
 we finally completed it!

SC3 B276.summary: A local contact approaches an informant at the tavern. Maria buys reliable timing and location details about the approaching mission.

speeches.Japanese: 親父、あの男はいるか？
speeches.English: Barkeep, is he here?

speeches.Japanese: …待ってな
speeches.English: Wait here.

speeches.Japanese:
おう、おめえか
どうした？
speeches.English: Oh, it's you. What's up?

speeches.Japanese:
あなたが情報屋ね
ポルトガルから来る宣教師の
一団のことを教えてほしいの
だけど
speeches.English:
You're the informant? I'd like 
 to know about the missionaries 
 coming from Portugal.

speeches.Japanese:
あん？
なんだい、この女は？
speeches.English: Huh? Who is this woman?

speeches.Japanese: 俺の新しいボスだ
speeches.English: My new boss.

speeches.Japanese:
タダで教える情報はねえぜ
金貨１０００枚払えるのかい？
speeches.English:
Nothing is free. Can you pay 
 1,000 coins?

speeches.Japanese: いいわ
speeches.English: Yes.

speeches.Japanese:
よし、教えてやろう
船団が到着するのは明日
場所はこのマカオだ
speeches.English:
Good. They arrive tomorrow, right
 here in Macao.

speeches.Japanese: おい、本当だろうな？
speeches.English: You sure about that?

speeches.Japanese:
だますつもりなら、１週間後とか
杭州だとか、バレるまでに逃げられる
ような嘘をつくさ
speeches.English:
If I wanted to fool you, I'd say 
 next week, or Hangzhou. Something
 that'd give me time to run before
 you caught on.

speeches.Japanese:
よし、分かった
ありがとよ
speeches.English: All right. Thanks.

speeches.Japanese:
とにかく、俺はそのご一行様に
近づいてみる。元締めが会うなって
言う理由を確かめて
みなくちゃな
speeches.English:
Anyway, I'll try getting close 
 to those visitors. I've got to find
 out why the boss didn't want me
 meeting them.

speeches.Japanese: そうね
speeches.English: Right.

SC3 B278.summary: An apparent guard joins the arrest. The closing conversation reveals the ruse and the crew takes on the local contact.

speeches.Japanese:
我ら総勢１００余名
イエズス会より派遣され
ただいま到着いたしました
speeches.English:
More than a hundred of us have just
 arrived. We were sent
 by the Society of Jesus.

speeches.Japanese:
おお、ご苦労であった
後日の謁見にそなえ
ゆっくりと休むがよいぞ
speeches.English:
Thank you for coming. Rest well
 before your audience 
 in the coming days.

speeches.Japanese: 待て待てーい！！
speeches.English: Halt!
Eh?

speeches.Japanese:
我らをたばかり、おそれ多くも
天子までもあざむかんとする
薄汚い密売人ども！！
speeches.English:
Filthy smugglers! You dare 
 deceive us, and even the Son 
 of Heaven himself!

speeches.Japanese: な、何だと！？
speeches.English: W-what!?

speeches.Japanese:
だまされてはならぬぞ！
そやつらは、近隣にて悪事を
働く小悪党の集団！
speeches.English:
Do not be fooled! They are petty 
 thugs who prey upon this region!

speeches.Japanese: くそっ、どういうことだ！
speeches.English: Damn it! What's going on?

speeches.Japanese: ま、まことか！？
speeches.English: Truly!?

speeches.Japanese:
濡れ衣でごさいます！
我々は正真正銘の…
speeches.English:
These accusations are false! 
 We are genuine...

speeches.Japanese:
ええい、だまれだまれ！！
そなたらの顔を覚えておる者が
密告してきたのじゃ！
speeches.English:
Silence! A witness who remembers 
 your faces reported you!

speeches.Japanese:
まんまと宣教師の一団に化けおおせ
このマカオにやって来たまでは
よかったが、猿芝居もそこまでじゃ！
speeches.English:
You reached Macao disguised
 as missionaries, 
 but this farce is over!

speeches.Japanese:
さあ、もう言い逃れはできぬぞ！
全員、引っ捕らえよ！！
speeches.English: No more excuses! Arrest them all!

speeches.Japanese: おおう！！
speeches.English: Yes, sir!

speeches.Japanese: ヒャッホゥ！！
speeches.English: Yahoo!

speeches.Japanese: せやッ！
speeches.English: Hah!

speeches.Japanese: ひ、ひいっ！
speeches.English: Eek!

speeches.Japanese:
チッ！
こんなところで、捕まるかよ！
speeches.English: Tch! I'm not getting caught here!

speeches.Japanese:
うーむ…。すっかりだまされて
危うくわしの首が飛ぶところであった
そなたらのおかげ……ん？
speeches.English:
Hmm... I was completely
 taken in. I nearly lost my head! 
 It is all thanks to you... Hm?

speeches.Japanese:
密売人の正体をあばいた軍勢は
どこへ消えたのじゃ？
speeches.English:
Where did the troops who 
 exposed them go?

speeches.Japanese:
え？
もう引き上げていきましたよ
speeches.English: They already withdrew, sir.

speeches.Japanese:
あ、左様か。ほう…
わしに挨拶もなしに？
…？？
speeches.English:
Oh...
 They left without a word to me?

speeches.Japanese:
しかし…
最近の明軍に
西洋人や日本人がおるとは…？
speeches.English:
But... Since when have there 
 been Westerners and Japanese 
 in the Ming army?

speeches.Japanese:
あの…、あんなもんで
よかったでしょうか？
speeches.English: Was that performance good enough?

speeches.Japanese:
驚いたわ
堂に入ったものね
speeches.English: Very convincing.

speeches.Japanese:
いやあ、傑作、傑作！
あのときの連中の顔ときたらねえぜ！
speeches.English:
Ha! That was priceless!
 You should've seen their faces!

speeches.Japanese:
そうそう！
マカオ総督なんて
完全に信じちゃってたもんね！
speeches.English:
Yes! Even Macao's governor believed
 every word!

speeches.Japanese:
さすがは、もと役者
街一番の物真似の名人じゃ
speeches.English:
Just what I would expect 
 from a former actor. The finest
 mimic in town!

speeches.Japanese: 県令の真似だなんて、おそれ多くて…
speeches.English:
Impersonating a magistrate...
 I hardly dared.

speeches.Japanese:
仕方がなかったのよ
向こうが変装で来るなら
こちらも対抗するしかないわ
speeches.English:
We had no choice. They used
 disguises, so we answered in kind.

speeches.Japanese:
これで、密売人組織も
しばらくはおとなしくなるじゃろう
…さて、おぬしはどうする？
speeches.English:
The smugglers should lie low 
 for a while. What will you do now?

speeches.Japanese:
どうもこうもありませんや
こうなったら、他に行くあてもねえ
俺はここで働かせてもらいやすぜ
speeches.English:
What else can I do? I've got 
 nowhere else to go now. I'll stay
 and work for you.

speeches.Japanese: いいわ。よろしくね
speeches.English: Welcome aboard.
